title: Why Stress Makes It Hard To Learn New Things
hook: Your brain has a switch that turns off learning when you are stressed.

narration.text: Your brain has a switch that turns off learning when you are stressed.
When you are stressed, your body releases a hormone called cortisol.
This hormone can disrupt a key part of your brain: the hippocampus.
The hippocampus is vital for forming new memories and learning new information.
High cortisol levels can make it harder for your hippocampus to work effectively.
This means you struggle to absorb and remember new things.
It is not just you; it is your brain protecting itself from perceived threats.
Have you noticed learning becoming harder when you are under pressure?

description: Ever wondered why new information just does not stick when you are feeling overwhelmed? It is not just in your head. High stress levels can directly impact your brain's ability to learn and remember. This video explains how cortisol affects your hippocampus, making it harder to absorb new knowledge.
topic: Why you sometimes struggle to learn new things when you are stressed, explaining how cortisol affects the hippocampus.
